messages:
jin: thinking out loud — we need a small proxy in front of OTLP exporters that does two things: 1) redact/normalize span attributes (PII, long strings), and 2) map tenant_id -> vendor dataset/credentials so we can fanout to Honeycomb/Tempo/Datadog with per-tenant datasets. any objections?

tara: sounds reasonable. main questions: where does the mapping live? env config, k/v store, or a central service? and how do we ensure perf (extra hop) doesn't blow latency SLOs? :thinking_face:

mike: +1 for proxy. my vote: run as a sidecar in the ingest plane (colocated with otel-collector pool) rather than per-app sidecar. single hop inside infra, can scale horizontally. mapping in a small read-through cache backed by dynamo/consul. TTLs short so we can update dataset routing fast.

alyssa: re: redaction — we need a clear policy. redact by pattern and max-length, but also consider reversible hashing for tenant_id when teams need joinability across traces. reversible = BAD for PII. prefer keyed HMAC with per-org salt if any form of linkage is required. also check GDPR residency: route EU tenants to EU honeycomb/tempo endpoints.

jin: agreed on HMAC for non-PII linking. thought of config like: 
```yaml
processors:
  attribute_remap:
    drop:
      - user_email
      - credit_card
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: user_id
        action: hash
        salt_kms_ref: projects/prod/keys/tracing-salt
exporters:
  honeycomb/tempo:
    dynamic_dataset_from: attributes.tenant_id
```
This proxy would also enforce max-attr-size and truncate long string attrs, add retention markers. thoughts on enforcement vs best-effort?

tara: enforcement is safer: let teams know attribute gets dropped/truncated and emit a metric per drop. best-effort leads to silent PII leaks. also add telemetry for number of routed spans per backend (cost reasons).

mike: agree on metrics. implement sampling/token-bucket per-tenant so cheap tenants can't flood premium backends. for dynamic_dataset_from, be careful: Honeycomb requires X-Honeycomb-Team header per dataset — proxy must inject correct header and switch TLS certs if using region-specific endpoints.

alyssa: +1 on per-tenant quotas. Also ensure scrubbing runs before sampling if sampling uses attributes (so sample decisions are consistent). for EU routing: map tenant.locale or tenant.region attribute to endpoint override.

exporter-bot: config-check: new proxy config schema v1 passes lint, but note: attribute_remap.hash requires KMS access. will fail dry-run if no key configured.

jin: good call. ops/infra will provision key. any objections to building this in Go + small binary to sit in front of otel-collector? latency budget: <1ms median added per span in our staging perf tests.

tara: Go makes sense. also add a mode where the proxy can run in-process in the collector for simpler deployments (feature flag).

mike: one more operational note — retention tags: we should tag spans with a "retention_policy" attribute so downstream exporters and storage can apply TTL without guessing. e.g., retention:30d or retention:90d.

alyssa: and log a sampled example (sanitized) when dropping attributes so owners can triage. but keep that sample rate tiny.

jin: OK next steps: prototype proxy that does attribute-remap + dataset mapping + per-tenant quota. i'll sketch an implementation PR and a minimal otelcol config. thanks all. :thumbsup:

exporter-bot: canary-deploy started to staging/otel-proxy v0.1.0 at 1876543275
